points.why: It signs the loop (two opposite links and one same link, merging requests-to-overload-to-quality into one negative step), concludes it is reinforcing, and says the response itself is what overloads the labelers.
It identifies the lead's balancing loop (more labeled data raises accuracy if labels are good) and says which loop dominates depends on labeling capacity.
It never says the reinforcing loop can run upward with spare capacity (higher accuracy, fewer requests, better labels); it only frames the loop as amplifying drops.
It recommends capping intake at capacity, prioritizing informative examples via active learning, and tracking label quality with gold sets and audits.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly says that 'we always respond to drops' does not show self-correction, because the response feeds the problem.
